parsed.title: numeric token matches exact number, not prefix
parsed.detail: Comment claims "A pure number matches on the folder prefix" but the code does `folders.filter((folder) => folder.number === clean)` — exact equality. `unit-route 22` will not match folder `224-deterministic-replan-routing`, contradicting the documented resolution behavior.

parsed.title: slice(1,-1) drops the last cell when the row has no trailing pipe
parsed.detail: `cellsOf(line).slice(1, -1)` assumes a trailing `|`. For a well-formed row `| a | b |` cells are ["","a","b",""] and slice works, but for `| a | b` (no trailing pipe) cells are ["","a","b"] and slice(1,-1) yields ["a"], silently discarding the folded cell — the row is then skipped by the `cells.length < 7` check or mis-parsed.

parsed.title: roadmap/fix-index parsing does not handle escaped pipes, unlike ledger parsing
parsed.detail: `roadmapStatus` and `fixIndexStatus` use `line.split("|")` while the ledger parser `cellsOf` explicitly handles `\|` escapes. A roadmap or fix-index cell containing `\|` shifts the column indexes, so `cells[1]`/`cells[3]` read the wrong cells and the status can be wrong or "unknown". Two parsers in the same file disagree on Markdown table semantics.

parsed.title: localeCompare undermines the declared determinism
parsed.detail: Header says "sorted for determinism" and `unitFolders` sorts with `left.dir.localeCompare(right.dir)` — locale-dependent, so ordering (and thus match order, read-set tie-breaks, and the fingerprint input) can differ across environments with different locales, contradicting the module's determinism contract.

parsed.title: `..` substring check over-rejects legitimate paths
parsed.detail: `candidate.includes("..")` rejects any cited path containing the substring anywhere, e.g. a real file named `docs/fix/224-a..b/x.md` or `foo..bar.md` is silently dropped from the read set even though it exists and is safe; the check is meant to block traversal but path traversal is already impossible since candidates must `exists()` relative to PROJECT and cannot be absolute.
